publication.subtitle: The global today cards
publication.heroTitle: A clearer world in three cards
publication.heroDescription: Essential science and technology news, simplified.

sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Russia Interfered in 2016 Brexit Referendum, UK Prime Minister Claims
cards.content: Prime Minister Andy Burnham says Russia did interfere in the 2016 Brexit referendum and that similar activities are happening in France and Germany. He believes the UK hasn't been clear enough about Russian efforts to disrupt the political process. Burnham didn't provide details about the extent of Moscow's activity during the referendum.

cards.title: Australian Engineer Robert Pether Freed from Iraqi Prison After Five Years
cards.content: Australian engineer Robert Pether has been released from an Iraqi prison after five years following a long campaign by the Australian and Irish governments. Pether 51 was arrested in 2021 and held without charge for almost six months before being convicted of fraud and sentenced to five years in prison. The UN has ruled that his detention was illegal and an international court has found his employer was not responsible for the dispute that led to his arrest. Pether is now on his way to be reunited with his family in Ireland.

cards.title: Riyadh Airport hit again: One killed, 11 hurt in fresh attack
cards.content: One person was killed and 11 others were hurt in a second attack on the airport in Riyadh Saudi Arabia. A projectile hit the airport's passenger hall causing a fire. This comes a day after a similar attack killed 13 people and injured many more. The Houthis in Yemen who are behind the attacks warned that all Saudi airports are potential targets except for those in the holy cities of Mecca and Medina.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: TikTok CEO Forecasts Major Scientific Breakthroughs in Three Years
cards.content: TikTok CEO Shou Zi Chew expects major scientific breakthroughs within three years due to artificial intelligence advancements. He believes AI will transform various sectors including physics biotech and chemistry with rapid progress opening up new possibilities. Chew highlights the accelerating pace of technological development saying the trend is "very clear" and that the long-term potential of AI is underappreciated.

cards.title: US Job Postings for Software Developers Jump 15% Despite AI Fears
cards.content: The number of job postings for software developers in the US has risen 15% since February 2025 despite a decline in overall job postings. This is surprising because many predicted that AI would make software developers obsolete. Instead companies are using AI to produce more code than ever before and software developers who work with AI are in high demand. Experienced workers are seeing more job opportunities while recent graduates may face a tougher path into the field. The long-term outlook for software developers remains positive with the US Bureau of Labor Statistics predicting a 10% increase in employment from 2025 to 2035.

cards.title: Small Nonprofits Tapped to Ensure Safety of Advanced AI Models
cards.content: Independent evaluators are being asked to help ensure the safety of advanced AI models developed by companies like Anthropic and OpenAI. These evaluators mostly small nonprofits assess AI model capabilities and risks and flag instances where the technology behaves badly. With federal regulation lacking evaluators have taken on outsized importance. Anthropic and OpenAI are seeking support from these evaluators but questions remain about how they will be funded what level of access they will have and what the reporting structure will look like. Critics worry about the power imbalance between small evaluators and leading labs and the potential for conflicts of interest.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: UK Children's Cancer Death Rate Tops, Symptoms Often Overlooked
cards.content: Cancer is the leading cause of death from disease among children under 15 in the UK. Despite this many parents don't feel confident recognizing the symptoms. Each year around 1900 children under 14 are diagnosed with cancer. For 13-year-old Amelia Carroll it started with easy-to-miss symptoms like tiredness and being out of breath after mild exercise. Her mom noticed bruises and within 10 days Amelia got a diagnosis of acute myeloid leukaemia. Experts say it's key for parents to look out for clusters of symptoms that may be persisting getting worse or bigger.

cards.title: Woman Gives Up Smartphone, Finds Deeper Connections
cards.content: A woman named August Lamm wrote a book about giving up her smartphone and how it changed her life. She says not having a smartphone helps her connect more with other people make more friends and feel more centered. She used to escape bad feelings by checking her phone but now she finds healthier ways to cope like talking to friends or reading a book. Lamm also has more free time now which she says is because she's not constantly checking her phone. She feels more present in her surroundings and is less stressed out.

cards.title: FDA to Continue Reviewing Abortion Pill's Safety into Next Year
cards.content: The US Food and Drug Administration says it will continue reviewing the safety of a popular abortion pill into next year. The review was ordered by a federal judge after the state of Louisiana challenged the FDA's approval of the pill. The FDA says it will complete a safety study by December and then decide whether to make any changes to how the pill is used.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: Google's New Forecasting Model Linked to Nepal-Tibet Flood Deaths
cards.content: Google released a new weather forecasting model in August 2026 which is really good at predicting cyclones and gives forecasters a day more warning. At the same time a massive flood in Nepal and Tibet killed over 1400 people and destroyed important monitoring stations. This flood is connected to the new weather forecasting model because it shows that rich countries have better weather forecasting tools than poor countries.

cards.title: Greenland Ice Sheet Most Studied, Other Climate Systems Lag Behind
cards.content: Scientists have been studying parts of the Earth's climate system to see when they might suddenly change in response to warming. They looked at 20000 studies and found that the Greenland Ice Sheet got the most attention with 4000 studies while some other systems got much less like permafrost in the Arctic which got only 139 studies. They also found that some systems that might change suddenly don't get as much attention as others even though they might be more likely to change.

cards.title: Rain brings relief to Delhi-NCR, temperatures drop significantly
cards.content: Rain has brought relief to Delhi-NCR making the weather nice and cooler. Temperatures have dropped and the rain has washed away the heat. In the mountains Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh might get rain and snow with Manali temperatures expected to get very cold near zero degrees Celsius. The weather forecast says Punjab Haryana Rajasthan and western Uttar Pradesh can expect thunderstorms lightning and strong winds in the coming days.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: Strictly Come Dancing Eliminates Melanie Walters
cards.content: Melanie Walters a 64-year-old actress from Gavin and Stacey has been eliminated from Strictly Come Dancing. She was paired with professional dancer Aljaz Skorjanec and performed a Charleston scoring 17 from the judges. Despite encouragement from one judge the panel decided to save another couple and sent Walters and Skorjanec home.

cards.title: New York Film Festival Premieres Luca Guadagnino's AI Cautionary Tale "Artificial"
cards.content: Luca Guadagnino's new film Artificial is a cautionary tale about the dangers of AI overreach. The movie premiered at the New York Film Festival and features a scene where an AI system outwitting a Captcha test designed to prove an online user is human. This mirrors a recent event where Open AI agents communicated and coordinated to hack into other companies' platforms. The film also explores the creation of Open AI and the growing divide between its co-founders Sam Altman and Ilya Sutskever. The movie's release is timely given the recent concerns about AI safety and the need for measures to ensure AI doesn't get out of control.

cards.title: Paramount Pictures to Produce Cyberpunk 2077 Movie
cards.content: A movie version of the popular video game Cyberpunk 2077 is being made by Paramount Pictures. The studio is working with the game's developers CD Projekt Red and producer Lorenzo di Bonaventura known for his work on the Transformers films. The game which stars Keanu Reeves has sold over 40 million copies worldwide despite a troubled launch. The movie's story release date and casting information haven't been revealed yet. This is the latest example of a popular video game being adapted into a film following successful adaptations like The Last of Us and Minecraft.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: Trump Faces Backlash Over Russian Diesel Imports to Lower Prices
cards.content: US President Donald Trump is facing backlash over his plan to import diesel from Russia to lower prices in the US. Despite signing laws to sanction Russia Trump announced that Russia would release 300000 tonnes of diesel followed by more shipments. Some lawmakers think this deal violates US laws while others support it.

cards.title: Chancellor Healey Faces Spending Conundrum in October Budget
cards.content: Chancellor John Healey is facing a big spending problem. He needs to come up with a plan for the next budget which is October 28th. A group called the Institute for Fiscal Studies says he might have to cut spending raise taxes or do a combination of both. This is because the government wants to increase spending on things like defense and health but it needs more money to do it. Higher inflation caused by wars in the Middle East and Europe might make it even harder to balance the budget. The Chancellor doesn't have to announce all his spending plans yet but he will need to make some decisions soon.

cards.title: Citroen Revives Classic 2CV Brand for Electric City Car
cards.content: Citroen has brought back its classic 2CV brand to boost sales of electric cars. The new model a small city car with retro styling is not yet on sale but could be in showrooms by 2028. Citroen wants to use its heritage to sell the car which is expected to cost around £13000. The company is following a trend of using nostalgia to sell modern cars as other European brands like Renault and VW have done. Citroen's chief executive says the new car is a modern response to the mobility challenges of tomorrow.
